title: Plan phase P3: life and action systems
desc: Planner mode PLAN_PHASE P3. This phase holds seed tasks from the game plan (P0-023), and task.mjs phase-add does not mark a phase as unplanned, so this task is the planning step: every seed depends on it. Read the phase in harness/state/backlog.json (goal, exit, milestones), harness/state/next_phase_notes.md (the section for P3), GAME.md (pillars, capability list, the sections the phase needs), TECH.md, VERIFY.md "Writing acceptance criteria" and the knowledge files. Write 12 to 35 tasks to harness/state/plan_P3.json and add them with task.mjs add-json. Fold in the seed tasks already in the phase with task.mjs deps --add, task.mjs edit and task.mjs order: split a seed that is too big, never duplicate one. Every task names its pillar; every mission task carries the four fun criteria, the driving share check and the respect rule check; every area or art task carries the respect rule and its area sheet. Check the GAME.md capability list and say which items the phase builds. Then run task.mjs planned P3. For this phase the notes list the systems in build order (nav and lane graph export first) and the items moved here from the foundation phase (the combat foundation and police). The HUD build seed stays dependent on P1-003 (Show Anmol the HUD mockups): if he has not answered when this phase starts, put P1-003 first and plan everything else so it does not wait for the HUD. Pillar: base task, it plans the work that serves the pillars named in the phase goal.
accept: harness/state/plan_P3.json exists and the phase has 12 to 35 open tasks, each with a "Pillar:" line and checkable acceptance
Every seed task of the phase is folded in (kept, edited or split with a note), none duplicated

title: HUD build: the slice components
desc: Seed from the game plan. No HUD is built before Anmol has seen the mockups (decisions.md "HUD gets its own discovery (Anmol)"): this task depends on P1-003 and follows his answers in harness/design/HUD.md "Answers". Build the SLICE components of HUD.md "Component list" in game/ui/ in the signed look (STYLE_BIBLE.md "UI"): the minimap with the objective marker and police, health, the wanted level beacons, money, weapon and ammo, the goal line and the mission timer, speed in a vehicle, prompts, and the hide rules (story scenes, the map screen, pause). Fonts are OFL faces that cover Devanagari (HUD.md names Teko and Mukta), added with their licence to the credits data. Every element is readable through debug.hud. The stand-in HUD (game/ui/standin_hud.gd) is retired. The planner of P3 may split this seed (minimap and route guidance, wanted and combat, the mission cards). Pillar: three lives, one city (the HUD carries the lead, the goal and the wanted level of each life), and filmi, never cheap (quiet until needed).
accept: Driving pose (lookproof view hud_play): the HUD covers under 9% of the frame and nothing but world markers sits in the centre 40% by 50% box
Safe margins of at least 64 px left and right and 56 px top and bottom at 1920x1080; no text under 15 px at 1080p
Devanagari renders with correct conjuncts and matras: a shot of the place names in HUD.md "Checkable rules" is read against the mockups
The objective shows within 1 s of a mission start and after every new objective (event hud_objective with the text)
The beacon count equals the wanted level at every change and the state word matches seen or searching (scenario)
Every HUD element is readable through debug.hud (visible, text, value); the HUD and subtitles never cover the player (debug.shotProblems)
HUD frame cost is 0.1 ms GPU or less in the perf scenario (perf_budgets.json systems), or the measured number is recorded with a reason

The verifier reads 4 shots (driving, on foot, combat with wanted, mission passed) against HUD.md and Anmol's answers; npm run typecheck, npm test and node harness/bin/verify.mjs --quick are green, with no engine or console errors

title: Cutscene runtime: data-file scenes, one player, skip to a declared end state
desc: Seed from the game plan (owner: decisions.md "Cutscenes and story telling"; signed design: TECH.md "Story runtime (CS2, DG1, LIP2 then LIP1, FC2, SB1, SK1)"). The slice gets short in-engine scenes; the big directed cutscenes with lip sync and face sets are RELEASE and come with the acts once voices exist. game/story/cutscene_player.gd and game/camera/cutscene_camera.gd: a cutscene is a data file game/data/cutscenes/<id>.json with shots (camera mark, lens, move, length: cuts, push in, dolly, orbit, handheld sway), actor marks, library animation clip names, look-at targets, lines by id and events. One player runs them on the sim clock. The verifier can seek to any time. Every cutscene declares its end state (actors, vehicles, camera, mission flags, clock); skip is one button, always, and jumps there through the same code as a normal ending with a 0.3 s fade and a one-line recap; a checkpoint is saved when a cutscene starts. The HUD hides in story scenes. Build one test scene with two actors and three shots. Pillar: three lives, one city (the story of the three is told in scenes), and filmi, never cheap.
accept: Test: the test scene played to the end and the same scene skipped at 3 different times give the same end state (actors, vehicles, camera, flags, clock)

Scenario cutscene_seek: at 5 seeked times every actor named in the shot is inside the frame (a hook reports screen boxes), and across the whole scene no actor that the shot names leaves the frame; flakecheck 3 runs (5 when low usage mode is off)
Skip returns control in under 1 s of sim after the fade and writes the recap line; a checkpoint exists from the scene start
A schema test rejects a cutscene file with no declared end state

Cutscene and dialogue work together stays inside the 0.4 ms CPU line of perf_budgets.json systems (measured); npm run typecheck, npm test and node harness/bin/verify.mjs --quick are green, with no engine or console errors

title: Dialogue line player, Hinglish and English subtitles, and the jaw
desc: Seed from the game plan (TECH.md "Story runtime": DG1, SB1, LIP2; STORY_OUTLINE.md section 5 for the talk rules). game/story/dialogue_player.gd and subtitles.gd, with game/characters/face.gd for the jaw. A line is data in game/data/dialogue/ (id, speaker, channel, priority, text per language, voice file id, length), written by the content writer. Channels: drive talk, phone, inner voice, radio, ambient; one queue per channel. A crash, a chase start or a higher priority line pauses drive talk, which resumes with a short pickup line. Inner voice and radio duck under talk; the Dialogue bus ducks Music and Ambience. Subtitles: every line has a Hinglish text (Latin letters) and an English text from the start, with the speaker name and a colour per speaker, on by default, in Godot translation tables (CSV); a Devanagari track can be added later as a third language. Mouths: with a voice file the jaw follows its baked loudness curve; with none, a timed talk flap for as long as the subtitle shows. Lip sync from voice files and the small face set are RELEASE (LIP1, FC2) and are not built here. Voice lines are requests on the dashboard; text placeholders until then. Pillar: three lives, one city (most of the story is told in play: drive talk, phone, inner voice).
accept: Scenario dialogue_interrupt: a drive talk line is paused by a crash event within 0.2 s and resumes with a pickup line after the action ends; a higher priority line cuts in and the queue order is kept
Test: every line in game/data/dialogue/ has a Hinglish and an English text, a speaker and a length; no line is over 25 words
Subtitle shots in both languages are read by the verifier: speaker name and colour shown, text never over the player (debug.shotProblems), no missing glyph
The jaw moves while a line of its speaker shows and is still otherwise (hook reads the jaw value over a line with and without a voice file)
Ducking test on the audio buses: Music and Ambience drop while the Dialogue bus plays; npm run typecheck, npm test and node harness/bin/verify.mjs --quick are green, with no engine or console errors
